svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Resilience Hub's compliance status is the output of an estimator reading configuration, not a record of a recovery. Policy met is defined as the application being estimated to meet its RTO and RPO targets, and Policy breached as the application not being able to be estimated to meet them, so neither status describes a recovery anyone performed. The definition of Policy met itself adds that you are still expected to maintain a recover from a backup standard operating procedure and to test and time it. Three things bound the estimate. The policy's coverage, because RTO and RPO are entered per disruption type and the Region values are optional, so a green status can be silent on Region incidents while remaining a single value. The estimator's own floor, because a target of zero is accepted but the lowest possible assessment result is near zero, so a zero target always produces Policy breached. And the imported application definition, since the estimate is explicitly based on it. The four disruption types are Application, where infrastructure is healthy but the software stack does not operate as needed; Cloud Infrastructure, resolved by rebooting, recycling or reloading faulty components; AZ disruption, resolved by switching Availability Zone; and Region incident, resolved by switching Region, which is the only one whose target is optional. The four resource collection sources differ in what keeps the definition true: AWS Resource Groups is a stored query that changes on a tag edit, CloudFormation stacks change on deployment, Terraform state files are an S3 snapshot capped at 4 megabytes or 4,194,305 bytes, and myApplications is frozen because it no longer allows creating new applications or updating existing ones, while EKS clusters need namespaces added manually so an omitted namespace is outside the assessment. Drift detection compares against the previous assessment in which the component met the policy rather than the most recent assessment. The resiliency score measures how closely the application follows AWS recommendations for the policy, alarms, standard operating procedures and tests, which is recommendation adoption rather than resilience. Two quotas are not adjustable: one concurrent assessment per application, and a 365-day retention period for past assessments. The closing rule is to write the date of the last timed restore next to the status, and if the two disagree the restore is the one that is true.
svg.title: Policy met is an estimator's output, and its definition says so
svg.text: The status is an estimator’s output. Its own definition tells you to go and time it.
“You are still expected to maintain a recover from a backup standard operating procedure (SOP), and to test and time it.”
Policy met “estimated to meet its RTO and RPO targets”
Policy breached “could not be estimated to meet the RTO and RPO targets”
Neither describes a recovery. Both describe what an estimator concluded from configuration.
Three things bound the estimate
policy coverage Region RTO/RPO are OPTIONAL — green can be silent on Regions
estimator floor a target of 0 always breaches; the floor is “near zero”
what you imported “based on the imported application definition”
The status is one value, so none of the three omissions is visible in it.
Four disruption types — and the costliest one is the optional one
Application healthy infrastructure, software stack not operating as needed
Cloud Infra / AZ reboot, recycle or reload / switch Availability Zone
Region incident switch Region — target OPTIONAL
Four sources, four different things that keep the definition true
Resource Groups a stored query (#106) — changes on a tag edit
CloudFormation changes on a deployment
Terraform state an S3 snapshot, max 4 MB (4,194,305 bytes)
myApplications frozen (#107) — no new or updated applications
Two readings that mislead
Drift compares to the last passing assessment,
not the last one. And the score measures
recommendation adoption, not resilience.
The quotas that are fixed
1 concurrent assessment per application, so a
pipeline serialises. 365-day retention, so a
year-on-year trend must be exported first.
Write the date of your last timed restore next to the status, every time the status is reported.
If the two ever disagree, the restore is the one that is true. Estimated to meet and meets differ by everything that matters.
